_about: THE TEST ID INDEX — every test identifier we use, what it asserts, where it runs, and how to run it. Created 2026-08-08 (user) after MAINNETSMOKE-01 and TXS-1 were quoted in chat and could not be found anywhere: they were not tasks, and TXS-* existed only as prose inside QA-XFAIL1.json's `next` field. A test id must resolve to something you can open — that is what this file is for. Viewer: tests.html. Naming convention (PROTOCOL.md): a bare CAPITALISED reference is a kPad TASK; a test id is written T:<id> in prose and chat, and must come with its URL. Each suite records what_it_does (the actual steps), pass_means, fails_when, its dimension and its cost — added 2026-08-08 after the user pointed out that 'real value, real network, once a day' does not tell anyone what the test IS.

convention.task: BARE CAPS — a kPad task, e.g. TXSTATUS-CONSOLIDATE1. Look it up in kPad.
convention.test: T:<id> — a test case, e.g. T:HBARXFER-01. Defined in this file; results on the QA grid.
convention.assertion: T:<suite>.<n> — one assertion inside a suite, e.g. T:A5b.4. Never a task.

suites.title: The whole thing, end to end
suites.asserts: Two players join a board, one offers HBAR, both lock, the deal strikes, kWallet signs, it settles on Hedera.
suites.notes: Needs a game created on the TARGET's own backend — a board can only play a game its backend knows about, so pointing BASE elsewhere is not sufficient on its own.
what_it_does: Create a fresh public testnet game (own-to-own offers don't work, so every run needs a clean game two real players can join).
Player A opens the board and connects a wallet over WalletConnect — kWallet, our headless test wallet, does the pairing.
Player B opens the SAME board in a separate browser context and joins by typing an account (no wallet — a real second player).
A offers 0.01 HBAR to B via the asset card.
Both players lock. The deal strikes and the signing phase opens.
A taps Sign. kWallet auto-approves. The signature is saved and submitted.
The harness watches A's screen for the verdict toast.
suites.pass_means: A '🟩 Transaction successful' verdict appears on the board and the transfer is real on Hedera testnet. This is the only test that exercises the whole chain — board UI, lock rule, strike, WalletConnect, signing, submission, settlement, verdict.
suites.fails_when: Any link in that chain breaks. Historically its most common failure is harness fragility, not product breakage (see QA-HARNESSREPAIR1).

suites.title: Game is testnet, connector was built mainnet
suites.asserts: Rebuild for the right network, re-pair, sign — then reload and confirm it stayed right.
suites.schedule: cron, every 2h at :45 (offset from HBARXFER so they don't contend for kWallet)
what_it_does: Open a TESTNET game while the WC bundle has initialised for mainnet (its config default).
Tap Sign, forcing the bundle to rebuild the connector for the right network.
Re-pair and sign.
Reload the page and re-check.
suites.pass_means: The connector ends up on testnet with the right account, and STAYS there after a reload.
suites.fails_when: The bundle signs on a mainnet-scoped pairing — wrong-network signers, which is what WC-NETSCOPE1 fixed.

suites.title: Nothing stale survives a network switch
suites.asserts: After switching, only the correct account is connected and the old session is gone.
what_it_does: Switch networks with an existing session live.
Inspect the connected account list afterwards.
suites.pass_means: Only the correct account is connected; the old session is gone.
suites.fails_when: A stale session from the previous network survives the switch.

suites.title: The wallet killed the session and never told us
suites.asserts: You clear connections in HashPack while katomia is CLOSED. Signing must fail fast and honestly instead of hanging. Eight assertions, A5b.1-A5b.8.

assertions.asserts: GHOST successfully created (dApp believes, wallet does not)
sign against a ghost does not hang — must give up inside the tx's validity window, not at the 120s cap
assertions.history: FAILED at exactly 120.0s on lab1 AND production (2026-08-07); the frozen benchmark's only expected_fail. FIXED by TXSTATUS-CONSOLIDATE1 S4 (KWC snapshot 33993b7) — passes on lab1 and pat 2026-08-08. Fixture also corrected to a 40s validity window, matching the board's real one; the SDK default 120s made the <60s assertion unreachable regardless of bundle behaviour.

assertions.asserts: sign against a ghost fails loudly, never silently succeeds
user can re-pair out of the ghost state
sign after re-pair reaches the wallet on the NEW session

what_it_does: Pair with the wallet and establish a real session.
Snapshot the dApp's WalletConnect storage (IndexedDB).
Destroy the session WALLET-SIDE, then restore the snapshot — so the dApp still believes it is connected but the wallet has no record. This is a true 'ghost'.
Attempt to sign against that ghost.
Re-pair and sign again.
suites.pass_means: The ghost sign gives up quickly and loudly, inside the transaction's own validity window — never hangs, never silently 'succeeds'. Then the user can re-pair and sign normally.
suites.fails_when: It hangs (was 120s until TXSTATUS-CONSOLIDATE1 S4), or worse, resolves as if it worked.
suites.why_it_matters: This is the discriminating ghost test — it reproduces the exact scenario where a user clears connections in HashPack while katomia is closed. T:WC-A5-ONLINE passes even on broken bundles; this one does not.
suites.harness_note: lives on the box at /opt/kwallet/ (not web-served — it runs its own in-process wallet peer)

suites.title: The wallet was cleared while katomia was open
suites.asserts: The wallet's delete reaches us, so we should detect it and re-pair cleanly.
suites.state: 8/9 — A5.1-A5.8 all PASS (the ghost-recovery scenario itself is healthy). The single red is the newly-added A5.0, which is a genuine product defect (WC-RESETWEDGE1). Was SILENT for 14 days until 2026-08-08: an unbounded ensureNetwork hang ate the whole run, so it reported nothing — the silence was hiding BOTH a passing test and a real bug.
what_it_does: Pair, and sign once to prove the baseline works.
The USER CLEARS THE CONNECTION IN THEIR WALLET APP while the page is still open (simulated by a real wallet-side disconnect).
Try to sign again WITHOUT reloading and WITHOUT tapping Connect.
Re-pair and sign again.
Separately and last: call resetWalletLink(), reload, and re-initialise (assertion A5.0).
suites.pass_means: Step 3 detects the dead session, refuses to sign against it, and either self-heals onto a live session or reports KWC-GONE — never a silent wrong-session sign, never a hang.
suites.fails_when: The killed session survives in the dApp's storage and gets handed to every later sign (the pre-R2b bug: 'wallet says signed' then a wiped board).
suites.why_it_matters: Note this one passes on pre-fix bundles too, so treat it as a health check rather than proof the ghost handling works.
suites.harness_note: lives on the box at /opt/kwallet/ (not web-served — it runs its own in-process wallet peer)

assertions.asserts: wallet link resets cleanly — ensureNetwork settles after resetWalletLink()+reload
assertions.history: ADDED 2026-08-08. Currently FAILS: ensureNetwork never settles (45s ceiling hit). This is a REAL PRODUCT DEFECT, not a harness issue — reproduced in isolation. Tracked as WC-RESETWEDGE1. Runs LAST and in its own page so a wedge cannot take A5.1-A5.8 down with it.

assertions.asserts: dApp no longer reports a connected account after the wallet-side clear
no sign sent to the dead session
dApp surfaces an actionable error rather than hanging or lying
sign after recovery reaches the wallet on the NEW session

suites.title: The same board flow, on mainnet
suites.asserts: Real value, real network, once a day — the only test here that is not free to run.
suites.state: PASSING again as of 2026-08-08 08:20 (real mainnet transfer, consensus 1786177210.454269104). It was never a product failure: a failed run on 08-07 left its own unanswered pairing proposal in kwallet-mainnet, and the cron's 'skip if any pending item' guard then muted the test entirely — the grid showed '2 consecutive non-passes' when the truth was 'not run since'. Guard now ages pending items (only items <30m old block a run). Two older reds were harness flakes, not product: a #boardPlayerModal pointer-intercept on the lock click (08-06) and the #addAcctJoinAll account-landing race (08-07), both QA-HARNESSREPAIR1.
suites.dimension: MAINNET · full stack — a different dimension from everything else here
suites.cost: 0.01 real HBAR per run (~£0.002). The only test on this page that spends real money.
what_it_does: Create a real mainnet game.
Connect the mainnet wallet (kwallet-mainnet, a SEPARATE instance from the testnet one, on port 8791).
A second player joins by account id.
Offer 0.01 real HBAR, both lock, strike, sign, submit.
Confirm the result against the chain.
suites.pass_means: A real transfer reaches consensus on Hedera mainnet, with a real consensus timestamp.
suites.fails_when: Anything testnet cannot tell us about: mainnet node behaviour, real fees, the mainnet account's own state (e.g. the payer running dry), mainnet-only config.
suites.why_it_matters: Everything else here runs on testnet, where the system is thoroughly exercised and free. This test exists for the things that are only true on mainnet. A testnet-green / mainnet-red split is meaningful information, not a duplicate.

suites.title: Chip arrangement / visual layout
suites.state: not assessed in the 2026-08-07 benchmark pass — visual class, not a signing test.
what_it_does: Drive the board through a scripted set of chip moves.
Compare the resulting layout.
suites.pass_means: Chips land where the layout rules say they should.
suites.fails_when: A layout or arrangement regression. Not a signing test — it does not belong on the kWallet page.

suites.title: Domain send flow
what_it_does: Exercise the domain send flow end to end.

suites.title: Transaction validity-duration decode matrix
suites.asserts: 12 cases: Long int64 decode, SignedTransaction wrapper, cross-shape misuse fallbacks, absent field, garbage, real production fixture bytes, expiry arithmetic.
suites.reports: stdout only — not on the grid
what_it_does: Feed 12 shapes of transaction bytes to the validity-duration decoders: Long int64, SignedTransaction wrapper, cross-shape misuse, absent field, garbage, real production fixture bytes, and the expiry arithmetic.
suites.pass_means: All 12 decode to the right duration or fall back safely.
suites.fails_when: A decoder silently returns the wrong window — which is how a transaction's real deadline and the UI's idea of it drift apart.

expected_fail._about: QA-XFAIL1: assertions written to FAIL today, each mapped to the stage of TXSTATUS-CONSOLIDATE1 that should turn it green, so a red does not read as a regression. Only A5b.4 was ever automated; the TXS-* below are specified but NOT YET IMPLEMENTED as harnesses — that is the open half of QA-XFAIL1.

cases.asserts: An abandoned Sign tap never produces a user-visible message after the transaction it belonged to is dead. (Tap Sign, abandon, complete a DIFFERENT tx, wait past 120s.)
cases.status: specified, not automated; behaviour fixed by S2 — mechanics covered by the S2 synthetic suite

cases.asserts: Every transaction message names its txid, including board:sign:error's kdiag payload.
cases.status: specified, not automated; fixed by S2 (txid+accountId added)

cases.asserts: Two board tabs: a verdict shown in one can never be re-declared by the other.
cases.status: specified, not automated; fixed by S2 (localStorage re-read + BroadcastChannel)

cases.asserts: A failure verdict arrives within 15s of expiry. Measured pre-fix: 57-62s.
cases.status: fixed by S3 — measured 14.0s e2e on lab1 2026-08-07

cases.asserts: No full-board wiper plays for a verdict older than a few seconds, or once a newer signing window has opened.
A negative signal followed by a positive one within ~1.2s shows success only (the settle window).
cases.status: fixed by S2 — covered by the S2 synthetic suite

cases.asserts: A success verdict records its provenance — mirror node vs socket.
cases.status: implemented by S5 (⚡ socket / ⛓ mirror / 🛰 backend glyph); no automated assertion yet

cases.asserts: Order-mode expiry comes from the backend window, not a hardcoded 2m30s client clock.
cases.status: fixed by S7 — guess deleted; no automated assertion yet

cases.asserts: A sign against a dead session gives up inside the transaction's validity window, not at 120s.
cases.status: AUTOMATED and now PASSING — see T:WC-A5B-GHOST above

not_covered_by_automation: mobile sign with the wallet backgrounded (kWallet is always awake — it cannot fail this)
HashPack's own session lifecycle by hand (extension vs mobile app)
animation and timing judgement — whether the wiper/confetti lands at the right moment
